title: Covering arrays CAN(t,k,v)
keeper: C. Smolen's ca-tools table (github.com/chrispbsmolen/ca-tools), the live successor of C. J. Colbourn's covering array tables
revision: table/ca_table.csv at commit 0e0bf0d (9 Nov 2026 03:36 UTC), 15,112 rows

template.title: Covering array CAN({t},{k},{v})
template.statement: Find an array with {k} columns over {v} symbols (the integers below {v}) in which every {t} columns show all {v}^{t} tuples of symbols in some row (a covering array of strength {t}), with as few rows as possible.
template.submission: Text file: one row per line, {k} symbols (integers below {v}) separated by spaces.

score: the number of rows (smaller is better)
best_text: The best known size in the ca-tools table is {best} rows ({holder}); an array with fewer rows improves it.
bound_source: v^t, the number of tuples every t columns must show
holder_sources: the table's source of the row that gives the best value (by its own rule: the fewest rows among CITED and VERIFIED rows with at least k columns)
open_rule: every row of the table (CITED or VERIFIED) that is a step of its staircase (no row with more columns has as few rows), above v^t, leaving out strength 2 over 2 symbols (solved exactly by Kleitman and Spencer and by Katona)
left_out: 2190 rows beaten by a row with more columns; 134 cells solved (v^t rows, or t = v = 2); 9230 cells whose check would take more than 2 x 10^8 set intersections (C(k,t) v^t)
